pack.title: Daily Stack
pack.description: Eight handcrafted mixed-theme boards that rotate one per day.

categories.title: BREAKFAST CEREALS
categories.triviaFact: Muesli was developed around 1900 by the Swiss doctor Maximilian Bircher-Benner for his patients.

categories.title: TREES
categories.triviaFact: It takes roughly 40 liters of maple sap to make a single liter of maple syrup.

categories.title: VOLCANO WORDS
categories.triviaFact: Molten rock is called magma while underground and lava once it erupts onto the surface.

categories.title: ANAGRAMS OF FRUITS
categories.triviaFact: Rearranged, these words spell plum, grape, mango and peach.

redHerrings.note: ASH is what a volcano spews, but LAVA, MAGMA, CRATER and VENT complete the volcano words, and the trees need ASH.

categories.title: US STATES
categories.triviaFact: Maine is the only US state whose name has just one syllable.

categories.title: NEW YORK BOROUGHS
categories.triviaFact: Manhattan is the most densely populated of New York City's five boroughs.

categories.title: IVY LEAGUE SCHOOLS
categories.triviaFact: The Ivy League began as an athletic conference, formally created in 1954.

categories.title: ___ BREAD
categories.triviaFact: Irish soda bread rises with baking soda and buttermilk instead of yeast.

redHerrings.note: BROWN bread is real, but SODA, GINGER, CORN and SHORT complete the breads, and the Ivy League needs BROWN.
CORNELL starts with CORN, which can tempt you toward the breads, but it is the Ivy League university.

categories.title: BONES
categories.triviaFact: The femur, or thigh bone, is the longest and strongest bone in the human body.

categories.title: SENSES
categories.triviaFact: Much of what we call taste comes from smell, which is why food seems bland with a blocked nose.

categories.title: BASIC TASTES
categories.triviaFact: Umami, the savory flavor of broth and parmesan, was named by the Japanese chemist Kikunae Ikeda.

categories.title: WAYS TO TEASE
categories.triviaFact: Josh, meaning to tease playfully, has been used in American English since the 1800s.

redHerrings.note: To RIB someone means to tease them, but KID, JOSH, RAG and TAUNT already make four, so RIB stays with the bones.
TASTE sits naturally beside SWEET and SOUR, but it is one of the senses; the basic tastes are SWEET, SOUR, BITTER and UMAMI.

categories.title: SEA CREATURES
categories.triviaFact: A seahorse father carries the eggs in a pouch until the young are born.

categories.title: SHADES OF BLUE
categories.triviaFact: Indigo dye was so prized that it was traded as blue gold along ancient trade routes.

categories.title: PARTS OF A SHIP
categories.triviaFact: The keel is a ship's backbone, running along the bottom of the hull from bow to stern.

categories.title: ENGLISH PLACES THAT ARE ALSO WORDS
categories.triviaFact: Bath is named after its Roman baths, built around natural hot springs.

redHerrings.note: HULL is an English city and an ordinary word, but BATH, DERBY, READING and WELLS complete that set, and the ship needs its HULL.

categories.title: CARD SUITS
categories.triviaFact: The four French suits used on most playing cards today date from 15th-century France.

categories.title: CHESS TERMS
categories.triviaFact: Stalemate ends a chess game in a draw, even if one side has far more pieces.

categories.title: GEMSTONES
categories.triviaFact: Rubies and sapphires are the same mineral, corundum, colored differently by trace elements.

categories.title: PROGRAMMING LANGUAGES
categories.triviaFact: Python is named after the comedy troupe Monty Python, not the snake.

redHerrings.note: RUBY is also a programming language, but PYTHON, JAVA, SWIFT and RUST complete that group, and the gemstones need RUBY.
DIAMONDS are the most famous gemstone, but here they are a card suit alongside HEARTS, SPADES and CLUBS.

categories.title: STRING INSTRUMENTS
categories.triviaFact: The sitar has sympathetic strings that are not plucked but vibrate along with the played ones.

categories.title: BALLROOM AND LATIN DANCES
categories.triviaFact: The tango grew up in the late 1800s in the port neighborhoods of Buenos Aires and Montevideo.

categories.title: NATO ALPHABET
categories.triviaFact: The NATO phonetic alphabet was adopted in the 1950s so radio messages could be understood across languages.

categories.title: ___CHAIR
categories.triviaFact: A highchair raises a small child to table height so they can eat alongside adults.

redHerrings.note: TANGO and FOXTROT are NATO code words, but BRAVO, HOTEL, KILO and JULIET complete that alphabet group, and the dances need both.

categories.title: MOONS
categories.triviaFact: Ganymede, which orbits Jupiter, is the largest moon in the solar system and bigger than the planet Mercury.

categories.title: SPACE PIONEERS
categories.triviaFact: Valentina Tereshkova became the first woman in space in 1963, orbiting Earth 48 times.

categories.title: BRIGHT STARS
categories.triviaFact: Sirius is the brightest star in the night sky, about 8.6 light-years from Earth.

categories.title: HIDDEN CAR BRANDS
categories.triviaFact: Audi is Latin for listen, a pun on founder August Horch, whose surname means listen in German.

redHerrings.note: POLARIS is also a vehicle maker, but it is not hidden inside a longer word; here it is the North Star.
TITAN suggests a mythic giant or a rocket, but it is Saturn's largest moon and completes the moons group.

categories.title: KITCHEN APPLIANCES
categories.triviaFact: The microwave oven grew out of radar research after engineer Percy Spencer noticed a candy bar melting.

categories.title: CHEESES
categories.triviaFact: Feta is a protected name in the EU, reserved for brined cheese from Greece made with sheep or goat milk.

categories.title: TYPES OF DRUM
categories.triviaFact: The tabla is a pair of hand drums central to the classical music of northern India.

categories.title: READ BACKWARDS FOR A NEW WORD
categories.triviaFact: Words that spell a different word in reverse, like drawer and reward, are called semordnilaps.

redHerrings.note: A KETTLE drum is a real instrument, but SNARE, BONGO, TABLA and CONGA complete the drums, and the appliances need KETTLE.
EDAM reads MADE backwards, but DRAWER, STRESSED, SPOOL and PART complete that set, and the cheeses need EDAM.
